profile.address: Leaf Lake Parkway, Wheeling Crossroad, Birmingham, Jefferson County, Alabama, 35020
profile.reading:
This facility sits along Leaf Lake Parkway near Wheeling Crossroad in the Birmingham area of Jefferson County, Alabama, and its name traces back to Sungard Availability Services, once one of the larger names in enterprise disaster recovery and colocation services. Sungard AS built its business on a network described in company materials as roughly 75 hardened data centers spread across a dozen countries, but the company's own public materials do not break that network down by naming individual facility addresses, which is why no site specific technical detail for this Birmingham location has ever been publicly available, even at the company's peak.

Sungard AS's more recent history is directly relevant to understanding the current status of this building. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in April 2022, its second bankruptcy filing after an earlier 2019 restructuring, and it did not survive as a standalone company. Asset sales completed on November 3, 2022 split the business three ways. 11:11 Systems acquired Sungard AS's North American recovery, cloud, and managed services operations along with four of its data centers, 365 Data Centers acquired most of the remaining U.S. colocation business along with eight data centers, and four other facilities that were not part of either sale were wound down during 2023.

Which of those three outcomes applied to this specific Birmingham site is not established by any primary source identified in this research. A check of both successor companies' current public facility listings is informative on that point, however. As of September 2026, 11:11 Systems' published list of data center and cloud region locations does not include Birmingham, Alabama, and 365 Data Centers' published list of its sixteen colocation facilities likewise does not include an Alabama site. Neither absence is a formal confirmation of closure, since a company's public marketing page is not a complete inventory of every facility it operates, but taken together they make it considerably more likely that this Birmingham building was among the facilities wound down in 2023 rather than one retained by either acquiring company.

One other clarification is worth stating plainly for anyone researching data centers in this part of Jefferson County. This Sungard facility is a separate property from Nebius's planned BHM01 campus, a much larger 300 megawatt project reported at 201 Milan Parkway, the former Regions Lakeshore Operations Center, roughly 3.9 kilometers away. At least one industry aggregator has been observed misattributing BHM01's capacity to this Sungard site, an error worth correcting given how different the two projects are in scale, ownership, and current operating status.

This facility in Birmingham cannot be assessed for AI relevance because no published capacity figure exists. It traces to Sungard Availability Services, a company that operated roughly 75 hardened data centers globally but never published site-specific technical details, and which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2022. The research record found no public specification for this location's power capacity, square footage, cooling capability, or current operating status.

The facility's current ownership is unresolved. Sungard AS completed asset sales on November 3, 2022, splitting its business three ways: 11:11 Systems took four data centers and recovery services, 365 Data Centers took eight colocation facilities, and four remaining sites were wound down in 2023. As of September 2026, neither 11:11 Systems nor 365 Data Centers lists a Birmingham, Alabama location in its published facility roster, making it more likely this site was among the four closed rather than retained, though neither absence constitutes formal confirmation.

This Birmingham site is separate from Nebius's planned BHM01 campus, a 300 megawatt project 3.9 kilometers away at the former Regions Lakeshore Operations Center. At least one industry aggregator has misattributed BHM01's capacity to this Sungard facility. Alabama has 12 mapped data center sites with 9.5 MW of published capacity across two facilities, and this site ranks third by published capacity only because its published capacity is zero.
